title: Eddie Jackson in the brass band and how crowds followed
summary: Crowds followed bands to the cemetery and Eddie Jackson's sousaphone could be heard for miles.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: And the people used to follow the band from the startin' to the finish. That's right. From the startin' to the finish. You go all the way to the graveyard, okay, you go up to Gretna, they go, go to Gretna, and back, you see? And all, and Eddie Jackson, you see, when Eddie Jackson was playing in the brass band, you could hear him for miles, you see? That's right, yeah. And them youngsters really know why they had to say, oh, they, they, somebody had blocks from here. They know, because they used to hear him. They hear him, you know what I mean? They hear that instrument and why they don't hear the others, you know what I mean?
He came from over the river too, didn't he?

Yeah, he came from over the river. He used to live on, I tell you where he used to live, he used to live on, over the track there, he's right there on, Frank Boyle's got a garage, right across the street there. That's Hancock's. Yeah. That's Hancock's.
